title: Planar universal optimality, tiered: kernel-checked consequences, a non-uniqueness theorem, and a CVODE N-body consistency check for the Yukawa interaction
description:
Version 2 adds a cover figure and four figures, all generated by make_figures.py from the result files and from snapshots that re-run published seeds and reproduce their energies exactly. It also adds the jellium (long-range, s = 1, 2D Wigner crystal) extension's preregistration and Ewald controls, and laboratory protocols L1–L4 (Tier C proposals) with a shared analysis script. No v1 result changed. v2 was audited by a separate model instance (accept with corrections, all applied).

The openai/math release contains a Lean 4 proof that the triangular lattice minimises the lower g-energy among all locally finite planar configurations of density one, for every smooth completely monotone g. Every claim is filed in an Elenchus claim ledger (22 claims) with tiers A (kernel-checked), L (literature), C (argument) and X (floating-point exploration, never supporting a claim).

Tier A, conditional on the fidelity of upstream's definitions:

  • the rescaled triangular lattice is universally optimal at every density, in CKMRV's Definition 1.3 sense with upstream's lower energy;
  • universal optima are not unique among all configurations: the lattice with one vacancy is another, and it is not an isometric image of the lattice.

Tier X: a preregistered CVODE N-body study for the 2D Yukawa interaction.

  • No relaxed periodic configuration fell below the triangular-lattice energy (0/100 relaxations at kappa = 2, 0/50 at kappa = 1).
  • Annealing reached the lattice narrowly at kappa = 2 and failed the preregistered criterion at kappa = 1.

Jellium extension: Ewald energies match the published Madelung values (Alves et al. 2021; Bonsall & Maradudin 1977) to 2.6e-10 (triangular) and 4.3e-10 (square), and the square lattice is a saddle point. Its relaxation study is reported separately.

Laboratory protocols are proposed for four systems:

  • superparamagnetic colloids, whose 1/r^3 law is Riesz s = 3, in the theorem's class;
  • dusty-plasma monolayers;
  • colloids confined in cavities;
  • electrons on liquid helium.

The ledger gate reports 0 blocking findings and 6 flags (unaudited statement adequacy); the author chose to publish with those flags open and to seek community review. The work was produced by AI agents (Claude) under the author's direction; the author is responsible for the content.
notes: Preprint v2 (v1: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23293112). Figures, jellium-extension controls and laboratory protocols added; no v1 result changed. Lean: AutoevolveAI formal_cert/Triangular (LeanMaster v3.48.1). Numerics: rusty-SUNDIALS PR #72 and branch physics/jellium-wigner-2026-10-11.
